graph.record_definition: design: (node pair, canonical geometry, travel_time, cost)
graph.merge_note: `symmetrise` copies the data dict exactly, so a walk graph's forward/reverse pair has identical weights and collapses into one bidirectional record under BOTH definitions. The difference between the two counts is therefore parallel roads carrying DIFFERENT weights, which design §2.4 requires be kept apart because grouping must not answer a ranking question. The first run of this pilot attached to the production grouping and its prevalence counts are superseded (Codex pass 36 F4).

exact.note: point counts except the three named `..._candidates`

impact_bound.bounds: OBJECTIVE 1 only -- min over options of total travel time, which is the objective E1 is defined against (design §2.1). Moving an attachment along one record trades one endpoint's partial traversal against the other's by |delta arc| / L * T, so the minimum moves by no more than that.
impact_bound.does_not_bound: OBJECTIVE 2, the time along the COST-minimising path: selection by cost and reporting by time means a 0.013 s cost change can switch the route and move the reported time by 120 s (Codex pass 36 F2). Nor does it bound route AVAILABILITY, so one-way records are excluded and counted.

subdivision.note: TWO lawful re-expressions of every record in the point's band window, neither moving the road, changing its length or altering which traversals are legal: `subdivide` inserts every segment's midpoint, and `split_midpoint` expresses each record as two cut at its arclength midpoint, and `split_every_segment` makes every segment its own record. All three are reported because they penalise different conventions -- reporting only the first would be choosing the transformation that makes the incumbent look worst. Drawn at RANDOM with the seed below; the first version took a prefix, which on the two censuses is id or row order and so a spatial bias, and a rate from a biased slice is not a rate. Kept out of the population estimates above: this is a transformation diagnostic on its own sample.
